body.statement: Let \(k,p,q\in\mathbb N_0\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{k\times p}\) and \(D\in\mathbb R^{k\times q}\), and let \(\mathscr L_{\mathrm{ng}}(A)\) be the set of laws of \(A\xi\) as the coordinates of \(\xi\) range over arbitrary mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian real laws, with no location or moment restriction.  Then \(\mathscr L_{\mathrm{ng}}(A)\subseteq\mathscr L_{\mathrm{ng}}(D)\) if and only if there are a surjection \(f:U_A\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero real numbers \(a_i\), \(i\in U_A\), such that \(A_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\) for every \(i\in U_A\).  This includes \(k=0\), empty source families, and zero columns.
body.proof_tex:
For necessity, apply the assumed containment to the two-point source vector \(\xi^A\) furnished by \(\text{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\).  Its law must have a representation \(D\eta\) by independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources, so that lemma gives exactly the asserted surjection and proportionalities.

Conversely, suppose \(f\) and \((a_i)\) exist, and fix any admissible source vector \(\xi\) for \(A\).  For \(j\in U_D\), define
\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\xi_i.                                    \tag{4}
\]
The nonempty fibers of the surjection are disjoint, so the variables in (4) are mutually independent.  Every summand is nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  The lemma \(\text{lem:independent-sum-nondegenerate}\) shows that \(\eta_j\) is nonconstant.  If \(\eta_j\) were Gaussian, the L\'evy--Cram\'er decomposition in \(\text{lem:levy-cramer-decomposition}\), applied inductively, would make every nonconstant summand \(a_i\xi_i\) Gaussian, contradicting admissibility.  Thus each \(\eta_j\) is non-Gaussian.  Give every zero column of \(D\) an arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian source, independent also of (4).  Columnwise proportionality yields
\[
 D\eta
 =\sum_{j\in U_D}D_{:,j}\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\xi_i
 =\sum_{i\in U_A}A_{:,i}\xi_i
 =A\xi.
\]
This constructs a target representation for every source law without using expectations, variances, or location normalizations.  The empty cases reduce to the unique law at the origin and the empty surjection, as in the diagnostic lemma.
